main_text.p: cere in putrefcente materia. At interdum fieri poteft,ut ea uis non fit omnio imbecil la,fed humor putrefcens maxime eft uitia- tus.Hæc Galenus,quibus humores nó simpliciter,fed uarijs modis poffe putrefcere docemur. Quare qui à ueneno peftis eft corruptus fanguis illam non acquirit pu- tredinem, quæ concoqui & à natura uinci pofsit,fed aliam malignam, quæ exitiosas febres parit. Veruntamen peftilentium fe- brium alias alijs effe perniciofiores (prout magis, aut minus eft corruptus fanguis & uenenatus ) ex fymptomatis & incidenti- bus facile quis poteft percipere. Propterea hæ malignæ funt omnes, quæ carbunculos, & bubones antecedunt: ut & hæ in quibus ægri continuo metu aguntur, & cibum omnino faftidiunt. Contrà animi fecuritas, & ad cibum obedientia falutem fæpe denunciat: Veruntamen id nó eft perpetuu. Etenim nonnulli funt, qui ad quartum,aut quintum ufq; diem, ceu conualefcetes per domum oberrant,nec cibos refpuunt, qui tamen paulò pòft occidunt. Propterea omnium peftilentium febrium exitus anceps semper eft.Præterea totius corporis iacta- tio inquietudo q; magnum minatur pericu- lum.

page.notes: Handwritten marks in the left margin (apparently "peste" and "riores" or similar) are manuscript annotation, not printed text, and are left out. A brown ink stain covers part of the text near "quae concoqui" and "fanguis"; the words under it are read as printed. "nó simpliciter": the line break falls inside the word with no printed hyphen, and the first letters are slightly unclear. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so "exitiofas" is given as "exitiosas". The word "fe-brium" at the line end is read as "febrium".
